card.name: Abayı
card.era: Traditional; melody composed by Shaki composers
card.tagline: Shaki's comic dance poking fun at middle age
card.profile: Abayı (Azerbaijani: Abayı) is an Azerbaijani folk dance originating in the Shaki and Zaqatala regions, whose subject is middle age — in this area middle-aged people are called "Abayı" — and which is performed with slightly exaggerated, comic movements at a slow tempo (Wikipedia; Azerbaijani dances). Its melody was written by Shaki composers; once a group dance, it later evolved into a solo form, traditionally accompanied by instruments such as the tar, kamancha, saz and daf.
card.insight: Abayı is a rare example of gently satirical folk dance: by exaggerating the gestures of the middle-aged, it turns the dignity of age into affectionate comedy, reflecting the regional humor of the Shaki–Zaqatala area (Wikipedia).
